  1. net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api

Your first effect

Make Minecraft text use a custom color or animation. Start by trying a preset in the effect gallery, then register a name that your mod can put in formatted text. Keep the returned registration handle if you will remove that name later.

Open the effect gallery

Open Mods → Chromatic Codes → Config → Effects → Named → Effect gallery, or press F8. Named effects contains all 28 editable bundled styles, one per movement, including Phoenix, Direct gradient and Discord gradient. The gallery uses those same definitions. Adding, renaming, changing or deleting a definition updates both views; there is no fallback catalog.

General → Bundled styles is enabled by default. Turn it off to disable bundled colors and effects while retaining custom entries. Definitions stay editable. Re-enabling does not restore entries that you deleted and saved.

Cards fit the available width while preserving readable samples at low GUI scales. All cells share a uniform height with room for large trails. Change their width or height, search by name or movement, and scroll extra rows. Each animated card has playback controls. Shift-click + or − changes every card by one step relative to its own speed, including filtered cards. Space pauses all previews, R resets playback, M enlarges Matrix rain when present, and Esc returns to settings.

Use … to edit a configured effect's options. The bordered panel has a draggable scrollbar; Tab reaches every field and Enter validates the change. Option edits stay in the settings draft until Save & close. Cancel leaves the configuration file unchanged. Effects registered by another mod or script are previewed without modifying its callbacks.

Use a card’s corner x to arm deletion. Its background turns red over 300 ms; click again after the transition to confirm. Clicking elsewhere cancels. Shift-click arms all delete buttons with one synchronized red tween, including scrolled-out entries (and filtered cards in the gallery). After the tween, Shift-click again deletes all; a normal click deletes only that entry and leaves the others armed. Named styles are removed from the unsaved draft. After Save, deleted definitions are removed from the registry and stay removed across reloads. Only external previews are hidden until R restores them; their addon registrations are not changed. Back and Escape return through visited settings pages before leaving the config.

Ctrl+Z undoes edits, creations, toggles and deletions in the current settings session. A bulk deletion is one undo step. While editing a field, undo first restores uncommitted typing. Save is still required to publish restored definitions.

OffscreenCleanroom 0.1.1 is optional. With it installed, Shift+F8 or Pop out in Named effects opens a separate, resizable desktop window showing live registered effects. Closing that window leaves Minecraft open. Its preview controls do not write configuration.

To use a TTF or OTF resource pack in the gallery and in Minecraft text, follow Use a custom typeface.

Try a built-in preset

The default configuration includes named presets. Write &[rainbow]Hello§r for a waving rainbow greeting. The final §r restores ordinary formatting. Both & and § introduce codes.

Use these codes in text drawn by Minecraft's FontRenderer. Some input fields strip formatting, and mods with their own text renderer may bypass the effects. If a code appears as ordinary text, follow the renderer and input checks.

An inline code defines the effect directly in the text. For example, &[~wave:FF0000,0000FF]Hello§r needs no named preset. Inline codes must be enabled in the client settings.

Register your own color

The Java and Kotlin examples use ChromaticDefinitions and Minecraft's net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation. Give the entry an ID in your mod's namespace, such as your_mod:gold. The separate trigger gold is what you write in text as &[gold].

Keep the returned registration if your mod or script needs to remove this entry later. The final close() call in each color example shows cleanup. Run it when removing the entry; calling it during setup removes the color immediately.

Closing an older registration leaves any replacement in place. Closing the replacement removes it without restoring the earlier entry. See registration lifetime and batch cleanup.

var registration = ChromaticDefinitions.register(
        ChromaticDefinitions.Kind.COLOR_NAME,
        new ResourceLocation("your_mod", "gold"),
        "gold", 0xFFCC00, null);
// Text using this name: &[gold]Golden text§r
// Later, when unloading this declaration:
registration.close();

val registration = ChromaticDefinitions.register(
    ChromaticDefinitions.Kind.COLOR_NAME,
    ResourceLocation("your_mod", "gold"),
    "gold", 0xFFCC00, null
)

// Later, when unloading this declaration:
registration.close()

# Add this entry to the existing namedColors list in chromatic_codes.cfg:
[gold]:FFCC00
# Then use &[gold]Golden text§r

The color is a six-digit RGB number: two hexadecimal digits each for red, green and blue. The API accepts the integer value; configuration palette entries use the hex digits.

Register a configured effect

Use MovementRegistry to create an effect from a movement ID, palette and controls, then register a trigger for it. These examples also use java.util.List and java.util.Map.

The library registers the built-in movements during its Forge construction event. Declare the library dependency so these factories are ready before your mod creates an effect.

var effect = MovementRegistry.create("wave", 1, 1,
        List.of(0xFF4000, 0xFFD000), 0.5f,
        Map.of("amplitudeY", 2.5, "wavelength", 72));
var registration = ChromaticDefinitions.register(
        ChromaticDefinitions.Kind.EFFECT_NAME,
        new ResourceLocation("your_mod", "warm_wave"),
        "warm_wave", null, effect);

val effect = MovementRegistry.create("wave", 1f, 1f,
    listOf(0xFF4000, 0xFFD000), 0.5f,
    mapOf("amplitudeY" to 2.5, "wavelength" to 72))
val registration = ChromaticDefinitions.register(
    ChromaticDefinitions.Kind.EFFECT_NAME,
    ResourceLocation("your_mod", "warm_wave"),
    "warm_wave", null, effect)

# Add to the existing namedGradients list:
[warm_wave]:0.5:1:1:wave;amplitudeY=2.5;wavelength=72:FF4000,FFD000

A playback speed of 0.5 runs the animation at half speed. It leaves the wave's size unchanged: amplitude is still measured in GUI pixels.

Configure an effect

This creates a wave effect with the supplied colors and vertical amplitude, then sets its playback speed independently. Each language produces the same effect. Creating it alone does not give text a code to use; register a name for it in the next example.

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.MovementRegistry;

var effect = MovementRegistry.create("wave", 1, 1,
    java.util.List.of(0xFF4000, 0xFFD000), 0.5f,
    java.util.Map.of("amplitudeY", 2.5));

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.*

val effect = textEffect("wave", listOf(0xFF4000, 0xFFD000),
    playbackSpeed = 0.5f, options = mapOf("amplitudeY" to 2.5))

def text = mods.chromatic_codes.text
def effect = text.effect('wave', [0xFF4000, 0xFFD000],
    1f, 1f, 0.5f, [amplitudeY: 2.5d])

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.scaladsl.Chromatic.*

val effect = net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.scaladsl.Chromatic.effect("wave",
    0xFF4000,
    0xFFD000)
  .option("amplitudeY", 2.5).speed(0.5f).build()

import mods.chromaticcodes.Text;

val effect = Text.effect("wave", [0xFF4000, 0xFFD000])
    .option("amplitudeY", 2.5).speed(0.5);

The selected effect checks these settings when it is created. Playback speed changes how fast time advances through the animation; it does not change the wave’s height or letter spacing. The meanings of the other speed controls depend on the effect. Built-in effect types are ready after mod construction; register a custom type before trying to create it.

Register a text code and remove it later

This registers a gold color and a wave effect under names your text can use. Choose IDs in your mod’s namespace and keep the returned registration objects. Call close() later when removing those entries, not immediately after setup. Groovy replaces its previous script registrations after a successful reload; CraftTweaker records the changes as startup actions.

import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation;
import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.ChromaticDefinitions;

var receipt = ChromaticDefinitions.register(ChromaticDefinitions.Kind.EFFECT_NAME,
    new ResourceLocation("my_mod", "warm_wave"), "warm_wave", null, effect);
// Later, when your contribution unloads:
receipt.close();

import net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation

val receipt = effectCode(ResourceLocation("my_mod", "warm_wave"), "warm_wave", effect)

// Later, when your contribution unloads:
receipt.close()

// In the reloadable script loader; do not manually call lifecycle hooks:
text.namedEffect('my_pack:warm_wave', 'warm_wave', effect)
text.color('my_pack:gold', 'gold', 0xFFCC00)

// Omitting these declarations from a successful reload removes this owner's entries.

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.scaladsl.Chromatic.*

val codes = definitions("my_mod") { text =>
  text.effect("warm_wave", effect)
  text.color("gold", 0xFFCC00)
}

// Later, on contribution unload:
codes.close()

Text.namedEffect("my_pack:warm_wave", "warm_wave", effect);
Text.color("my_pack:gold", "gold", 0xFFCC00);

// Explicitly remove only this facade's still-current contribution:
Text.remove("my_pack:warm_wave");

Closing a registration removes only the exact entry it installed. If another registration has replaced it, closing the older object leaves the new entry in place. Removing the replacement does not restore the displaced entry. A short try-with-resources or Kotlin use block around setup would remove your code as soon as that block ends.

Keep learning

Read the formatting rules for reset behavior and limits, or the configuration guide to use the library from another mod.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or settingArgumentsWhat it does
MovementRegistry.create(id, colorSpeed, moveSpeed, palette, animationSpeed, options)Effect ID; color/movement controls; RGB palette; playback multiplier; option mapChoose a built-in effect and its settings. Use the effect’s reference for supported option names and ranges.
ChromaticDefinitions.register(kind, id, trigger, color, effect)Entry kind; unique registration ID; text trigger; color/effectRegister the entry your text should select. Only supply the color or effect appropriate to that kind.
receipt.close()No argumentsRemove the entry installed by this receipt when your addon or script no longer needs it.
colorSpeed / moveSpeedFinite effect-specific controlsAdjust the selected effect’s color and movement behavior. Geometry settings remain independent of playback speed.
animationSpeedFinite multiplier from -32 to 32Change playback speed; a negative value reverses time and zero freezes it.
optionsMap of supported setting names to valuesOverride matching keys in the effect descriptor. Unsupported names and invalid ranges are rejected.

When you finish: Creating an effect does not register a text trigger. Retain the receipt through the tool/script lifetime and close it during teardown. Parsing and registration do not need a screen; calls to Minecraft’s font renderer run on the client thread.
